headline: Sundernagar man survives Nepal disaster, reunites with family
content: Shimla: Stranded for nearly 36 hours on a hilltop amid Bhote Koshi-Trishuli flash floods in Nepal, 50-year-old Gyan Singh of Maloh village in the Sundernagar sub-division of Mandi district has finally returned home safely.Rescued by the Nepalese Army in a helicopter operation on Aug 27, Gyan Singh’s return brought immense relief to his family, who had spent anxious hours fearing the worst. “A total of four Himachalis were working there in the power project. Three survived, while a youth from Una district, whose duty was nearer to the dam site, is still missing,” Singh said.Gyan Singh was working as a foreman at the power project in Nepal for the last eight months. He returned to India on Sept 1.Singh was on duty at the powerhouse when the disaster struck on Aug 26. A sudden surge of water swept through the area, forcing him and others to run towards a nearby hilltop for safety. “A total of 110 workers were inside the powerhouse. All of us, except the one stuck inside, were able to survive,” he said.Recounting the ordeal, Singh said there was no prior flood alert, and that the weather was also clear on Aug 26. “We left for duty around 7 am, and between 9:30 am and 9:45 am, as we heard a loud sound inside the powerhouse, everyone started shouting and running for their lives,” Singh recalled.There was a moment when we felt there was no way out as the water level surged suddenly. However, we refused to give up, said Singh. The place where we were putting up was located at a higher altitude, but it also got swept away, he added.The family of one of our engineers, including his one-and-a-half-year-old daughter, remains missing, Singh lamented.The Nepalese Army eventually reached the stranded group on the hilltop by helicopter, rescued them safely on Aug 27 and took them to Butwal. Later, they were transported to Kathmandu.Gyan Singh’s wife, Kalawati, said the family had been unable to contact him since Aug 26.
